title: introduce-prefill-horizon-cost-inspector-cli-and-telemetry-adapter
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adds a new CLI tool (rwi prefill-inspect) that computes tenant-level prefill horizon cost projections, suggests safe batching and quantization profiles, and ships a telemetry adapter for unit-econ snapshots. Backwards-compatible; disabled by default in private installs.
description:
Motivation: Teams need a low-friction way to understand the near-term cost impact of prefill/warmup strategies and to generate conservative batching/quant suggestions before applying changes to production. This PR introduces a lightweight CLI (rwi prefill-inspect) plus a telemetry adapter that converts sampled prefill traces into tenant-level 'horizon' cost projections and candidate default profiles.

What this does: - Adds a CLI that can run against stored telemetry or live sampling (+ dry-run) to compute: 1) projected token cost across a configurable horizon window (days), 2) recommended micro-batch shapes and cache retention defaults, 3) conservative quantization candidates with estimated quality impact bounds. - Produces an exportable JSON report and a compact human-readable summary. - Introduces a telemetry adapter to normalize sampled prefill traces into the inspector's canonical format (tenant, route, sample_distribution, kv_hit_rate, seq_len_histogram). - Includes 'safe-mode' that enforces guardrails (max-q-drop, latency-slo-preserve) and a preview flag --apply-suggestions=false for manual adoption.

Checklist: - [x] CLI binary and help docs - [x] Telemetry adapter + mapping tests - [x] Unit tests for cost projection math - [x] Integration test against synthetic workload - [x] Docs page and quickstart example - [x] CI linting and build

Commits (high level): - a1b3f87: initial CLI skeleton, arg parsing and subcommand plumbing - 3c9d2e4: implement horizon projection (tokenize, unit-econ model, decay window) - 7f2a11b: telemetry adapter and mapping layer for sampled prefill traces - 5e4b99c: safe-mode guardrails and quant suggestion heuristics - b8d0f22: docs, examples, and tests - 9f7c55d: fixes from review (privacy opt-out for telemetry sampling)

Files touched (high level): - cmd/rwi-prefill-inspect/main.go (new CLI entrypoint) - internal/prefill/inspector.go (projection engine) - internal/prefill/quant_suggester.go (conservative quant heuristics) - pkg/telemetry/adapter.go (sample -> canonical format) - docs/cli/prefill-inspector.md - deployment/telemetry/otel-mapping.yaml - tests/integration/prefill_inspector_test.go - Makefile, CI pipeline hook to run integration test in sandbox

Review thread summary: - Marcus: "Nice compact design. Please add explicit unit tests around the decay math edge cases (zero-prefill, spike bursts). Also add a flag to cap assumed token price for simulations (some tenants use custom pricing)." -> implemented in 3c9d2e4 and tests added in b8d0f22.

- Lena: "Telemetry mapping looks good; two privacy asks: (1) make the adapter default to aggregated histograms not raw prompts; (2) add an opt-out env var for private installs." -> Added aggregation and PRIVACY_OPT_OUT env handling in 9f7c55d. Lena approved after CI passed.

- Tomás: "Behavioral concern: quant suggestions should never be suggested for routes with latency SLO violations. Add a sentinel to skip those routes." -> Added safe-mode check and explicit skip with logging in 5e4b99c. Tomás provided an approval after integration test updated.

CI and QA: - First CI run failed lint (gofmt) and one flaky integration test (timing). Author fixed formatting and stabilized integration test by replacing wall-clock sleeps with controlled fake clock. Re-ran CI; all checks passed (unit, lint, integration sandbox). CI status summarized in the checks section below.

Checks summary: - golangci-lint: pass - unit-tests: pass - integration-sandbox: pass (rerun after flake) - docs-checker: pass - smoke: pass

Operational notes and rollout: - The CLI is shipped as an opt-in dev tool. For Hosted customers we plan a small internal runbook that recommends "run inspector with --horizon-days=7 --sample-rate=0.05 --apply-suggestions=false" before applying any defaults. - For Dedicated/Private installs the telemetry adapter is disabled by default; enable via deployment flag and set PRIVACY_OPT_OUT to true to avoid sending histograms to Redwood telemetry. - Suggestions are conservative: quantization recommendations are always accompanied by an estimated quality impact band and an automatic fallback to the previous model variant.

Backward compatibility and safety: - No API surface changes. No breaking changes. - The CLI reads telemetry snapshots only and does not mutate serving configs unless invoked explicitly with --apply-suggestions. - All suggestions require a confirmation file when used in automated pipelines.

Follow-ups: - Add a web UI tab in Console to visualize inspector reports (ENG-2190). - Hook inspector suggestions to the defaults-as-code workflow (later PR). - Expand quant suggestion heuristics with a small eval pipeline to estimate quality delta in a lightweight manner.

Merge: squash merged by Lena Ortiz on 2025-04-02 after approvals from Marcus Chen and Tomás Rivera.

Notes for reviewers digging into code: - Start at internal/prefill/inspector.go to see the projection pipeline: sample normalization -> unit econ estimator -> horizon decay -> recommendation generator. - Quant suggestion uses a conservative LUT based on model family and current token-sequence statistics; see internal/prefill/quant_suggester.go. - Telemetry adapter contains mapping logic and aggregation heuristics; mapping config is in deployment/telemetry/otel-mapping.yaml.

If you want to run locally: go build ./cmd/rwi-prefill-inspect && ./rwi-prefill-inspect --tenant tenant_123 --horizon-days 14 --sample-rate 0.02 --dry-run --output report.json

End of PR description.
